headline: New Liquid Treatment Stops Tooth Decay in Half of Baby Teeth
meta_description: A paintable liquid applied by dentists halted decay in over half of cavities in a trial of 830 children under six, with reapplication every six months.
summary_short: A simple liquid treatment painted onto cavities stopped decay in more than half of affected baby teeth when tested on 830 young children.
body:
A liquid that dentists paint directly onto cavities has stopped tooth decay in more than half of affected baby teeth, according to a trial involving 830 children under six years old. The treatment takes only seconds to apply, making it practical for young patients who may struggle to sit still for longer procedures.

Reapplied every six months, this approach could spare many children from more invasive dental work. The finding offers hope for parents seeking gentler alternatives to traditional cavity treatment in early childhood, when dental anxiety can set the stage for a lifetime of oral health challenges. The simplicity and speed of application may also reduce stress for both children and their families during dental visits.
quick_facts: Trial included 830 children under six years old
Liquid stopped decay in more than half of affected baby teeth
Treatment takes seconds to apply by dentists
